claims.text: A specifically designed AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock with optimized particle-size distribution and chemistry, combined with tailored selective laser sintering, can reduce residual thermal stresses.
The proposed feedstock and tailored SLS process can improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed feedstock and tailored SLS process can reduce the processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes.
Particle-size distribution and feedstock chemistry are the structural mediators of the intervention.
Optimization of the powder feedstock and SLS process causes reduced thermal stress and improved mechanical properties.
The tailored SLS route operates under a lower thermal load than the conventional additive-manufacturing baseline.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the proposed route will produce components with improved mechanical properties.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, the proposed route will produce components with lower residual thermal stresses.
The proposed intervention is intended to apply to miniature-component geometries.
Exact processing-window parameters and test conditions cannot be specified from the available evidence.
Failure to improve mechanical properties and reduce residual thermal stresses relative to the conventional high-thermal-load control would falsify the hypothesis.
